chain.title: First Length of Wire
chain.desc: Iron ingots around a stone slab; the plain cable every other network part is built from or attached to.

chain.title: The Root of It All
chain.desc: A diamond and quartz on a cable make the Storage Network Root, the single block a network is organised around.

chain.title: Annexing the Chest
chain.desc: A wooden chest on a cable produces the Link Cable, which pulls an adjacent inventory into the network.

chain.title: A Face for the Network
chain.desc: A dropper and iron nuggets on a cable give the Storage Inventory, the first block that shows you what the network holds.

chain.title: Ordering From the Vault
chain.desc: Gold and a crafting table added to a storage inventory; the Request Table both browses and crafts from network contents.

chain.title: One Way In
chain.desc: A hopper on a cable, pulling items out of an attached inventory and into the network.

chain.title: One Way Out
chain.desc: A piston on a cable, pushing chosen items from the network into whatever it faces.

chain.title: The Gatekeeper
chain.desc: An observer on a cable makes the Filtered Link Cable, restricting which items a linked inventory contributes.

chain.title: Choosy Intake
chain.desc: A barrel on an import cable, so only the items you name are drawn into the network.

chain.title: Faster Ticks
chain.desc: Gold and redstone on a cable; slotted into a cable to raise how often it moves items.

chain.title: Whole Stacks at Once
chain.desc: Blaze powder and redstone on a cable, raising the number of items each operation carries.

chain.title: Keeping the Shelf Full
chain.desc: A chest and redstone on a cable, making an export cable maintain a target quantity instead of pushing endlessly.

chain.title: More Work per Pass
chain.desc: A comparator and redstone on a cable, increasing the number of separate operations a cable performs.

chain.title: Sweeping the Floor
chain.desc: A storage inventory with a speed upgrade and iron nuggets; the Collection Interface vacuums dropped items into the network.

chain.title: The Trade Window
chain.desc: A storage inventory with a stack upgrade and iron nuggets, giving a compact deposit-and-withdraw panel.

chain.title: The Bigger Counter
chain.desc: A copper block, an eye of ender and one each of the operation, speed and stack upgrades; a request table with far more room.

chain.title: The Vault in Your Pocket
chain.desc: Glowstone, gold and a slimeball around the network root, giving handheld access to everything the network holds.

chain.title: Reach and Grab
chain.desc: A cable added to the storage remote, letting you pull a specific item without opening the full list.

chain.title: A Magnet on Your Belt
chain.desc: An import cable added to the storage remote, sending items you walk over straight into the network.

chain.title: Placing From Storage
chain.desc: A request table added to the storage remote, feeding blocks to your hand as you build.

chain.title: The Wide View, Carried
chain.desc: A filtered import cable added to an expanded request table for the roomier interface in handheld form.

chain.title: Assembly Without a Bench
chain.desc: A gold block, an ender chest and a sea lantern around the network root; crafts from network contents anywhere.

notes:
25 of 26 item-model stems verified against item.storagenetwork.X / block.storagenetwork.X lang keys. All 24 recipe results resolve to modelled, named items. Note the German-derived registry spelling: every cable is 'kabel', never 'cable' (storagenetwork:storage_kabel, not storage_cable), while the DISPLAY names are English ('Link Cable'). Getting this backwards is the easy way to write a broken task.

DROPPED - storagenetwork:process_kabel. It has an item model but no lang key of any form and no recipe; it is the only model stem in the jar without a name. Left out as unobtainable/unfinished.

CAVEAT - storagenetwork:network_book is a registered, named item, but data/storagenetwork/recipes/network_book.json outputs patchouli:guide_book, not the mod's own item. With Patchouli installed a player following the recipe never receives storagenetwork:network_book, so it is deliberately kept out of both the chain and the wheels. Quest it only as a reward, never as a task.

CONSENSUS CONFLICTS:
1. moddb ends the mod on collector_remote (pos 1.000) with crafting_remote just before it at 0.893. The recipe graph reverses this: collector_remote is inventory_remote + import_kabel, while crafting_remote is the network root plus a gold BLOCK, an ender chest and a sea lantern - by far the most expensive item in the mod. Recipe graph preferred, so crafting_remote is the terminal step.
2. moddb orders storage_kabel (0.132), export_kabel (0.200) and import_kabel (0.300) all BEFORE master (0.314). The recipe graph is neutral here - all four are children of kabel - but nothing on a network functions until the root block exists, so master is placed second, immediately after the plain cable. This is a functional-dependency call, not a recipe-graph contradiction, and is flagged as a deviation.

The three wheels follow the mod's own three families: cables off kabel, the slot-in upgrades off speed_upgrade, and the handheld remotes off inventory_remote. crafting_remote appears both as the chain's final step and as a remote-wheel member, which is intentional - it is the capstone of that family.
